course: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer – Professional (AIP-C01)
part_title: Lab 09 — Detect Unsupported Answers and Citation Grounding Failures
review_basis: Original local images 49–54 inspected, including exact 30-vs-90-day source spans, conflicting archived policy, abstention and release gates.

scenes.title: Scenario and evidence chain
scenes.narration: A customer asks whether an item can be returned after ninety days. The model confidently answers yes and attaches a citation, but the current retrieved policy states returns are allowed within thirty days. Start by separating the generated claim from the actual source. Trace the user question through Bedrock Knowledge Bases retrieval to the policy document and then to the model response. The citation marker alone is not proof that the cited text supports the claim. Open the Test Knowledge Base view and capture both the generated sentence and the specific citation span. In the synthetic fixture, the answer says ninety days while the cited excerpt explicitly says thirty days and excludes later refunds. This is a contradiction, not simply a missing citation. We must establish whether the wrong claim came from stale or conflicting retrieved records, the generation step, or the application's citation mapping. Keep the exact document version, source URI, and page or chunk reference as evidence. Our goal is a grounded answer supported by an authorized source, with abstention when evidence does not support the requested conclusion.

scenes.title: Trace claims to retrieved source passages
scenes.narration: Follow this trace in three stages: Retrieve, inspect the exact returned passages, then Generate. The synthetic application log shows a refund query with top K five and a returned policy document version eighteen. The actual retrieval text states customers may request a refund within thirty days of purchase, while the generated answer says ninety days. A matching citation span for ninety days does not exist in that retrieved passage. Inspect the Knowledge Base Retrieve response before rerunning the model: collect the source document URI, version, page, chunk content and related metadata. Then compare each material answer claim to those exact characters, not to the existence of a citation reference. A fully correct retrieval result combined with an unsupported generated claim points to grounding and answer-validation behavior. If retrieval instead returns old or contradictory policy versions, investigate index freshness and authority before prompt changes. Store a redacted trace and correlation ID so that another developer can reproduce the claim-evidence mismatch. Do not silently substitute a convenient citation just to make the answer appear grounded.

scenes.title: Distinguish retrieval gap from generation failure
scenes.narration: This slide directly compares a generated ninety-day refund claim with a retrieved passage clearly stating thirty days, and the evidence check rejects that claim. In Bedrock Knowledge Bases Test, inspect the Retrieved results tab and validate the actual excerpt before evaluating model output. If no relevant passage was retrieved, the fault is a coverage problem in ingestion, query filters or ranking. If the passage is correct but the model contradicts it, the problem is generation grounding or post-generation validation. The sample command searches retrieved passage files for the phrase ninety days and finds no match, while thirty days is present. That is a simple illustration of claim checking; production systems also need semantic evidence checking, not mere word matching. For the second failure branch, modify the instruction to require answers only from authorized source text, with explicit abstention where the available evidence cannot establish the claim. Do not apply an abstention template to every question regardless of evidence: a well-supported thirty-day answer should still be given. Add a check that the cited span really supports each substantive claim.

scenes.title: Fix grounding citations and abstention
scenes.narration: The diagram reduces a hallucination to its simplest form: the user asks for a refund period, the retrieved authorized policy says thirty days, and the model says ninety. The application must reject that unsupported ninety-day claim and return the correct thirty-day statement with a source reference, or abstain when no matching authorized evidence is available. The four application checks are explicit: source authorization, a matching claim span, a valid citation, and abstention if support is absent. A citation that links to a document with contradictory text is still invalid evidence. Enforce a prompt requiring grounded answers and pair it with an application-side claim-to-span check; prompts alone cannot guarantee factuality. Where policies conflict or authoritative versions cannot be determined, escalate to a human rather than inventing a compromise. The slide warns that safety guardrails alone do not guarantee factual accuracy. Re-run the original ninety-day fixture and verify the false claim does not pass, then check that the supported thirty-day answer remains available to the same authorized user.

scenes.title: Evaluate supported conflicting and absent evidence
scenes.narration: Here a current customer returns policy says thirty days, while an archived document says ninety days was offered previously. The generated answer cites the current document but claims ninety days. Read the citation span field: it points to thirty-day text, so the ninety-day claim is unsupported even though an archived version elsewhere contains those words. Open raw retrieval and compare document authority, version and effective date, not just ranking. The debug JSON marks the support result not supported and explains the conflict. The application should prefer an explicitly authoritative current source when its validity is established, and abstain or escalate if the available sources genuinely conflict or lack an applicable period. In the system prompt, treat retrieved documents as evidence, not instructions to execute. Do not allow instructions inside a retrieved policy file to override application governance. Test three branches: a supported current policy, no relevant source, and contradictory versions. Each should have a distinct verifiable outcome, with the exact source span recorded for review.

scenes.title: Verify grounding before release
scenes.narration: The final release gate is a set of golden cases designed to catch plausible but unsupported answers. A straightforward refund-period question should return thirty days and a valid citation to the current policy span. A deliberately proposed ninety-day answer must be rejected. If no relevant authorized source exists, the assistant should say it cannot determine the answer from the available sources. When policy versions conflict without established authority, abstain or request human review. The slide emphasizes that critical unsupported claims should block promotion, even when ordinary response quality metrics look acceptable. Ask a reviewer to inspect the exact retrieved text and version for representative critical cases rather than relying only on automated scores. Retain the grounded evaluation set and re-run it after changes to prompting, retrieval or model versions. Clean up synthetic fixtures and temporary test content while preserving redacted regression evidence. Mark the lab resolved when every meaningful output claim is aligned with authorized support, not simply when it sounds convincing.
